subject: french
title: Application: Aller, Faire & -ER Verbs
welcome_lead: Add aller, faire, and the whole army of regular -er verbs to your toolkit.
meta_desc: GCSE French verbs aller, faire and regular -er verbs in the present.
final_note: With these, you can describe most of daily life en français.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Aller is irregular:

  • je vais
  • tu vas
  • il/elle/on va
  • nous allons
  • vous allez
  • ils/elles vont

It's also used for the near future: Je vais manger = I'm going to eat.

Faire means to do or to make:

  • je fais
  • tu fais
  • il/elle/on fait
  • nous faisons
  • vous faites
  • ils/elles font

Used for sports and weather: Je fais du foot. Il fait beau.

Most French verbs end in -er (e.g. parler, manger, regarder, écouter, habiter, jouer). To conjugate, drop the -er and add: -e, -es, -e, -ons, -ez, -ent.

Example with parler: je parle, tu parles, il parle, nous parlons, vous parlez, ils parlent. Note: -ent is silent!

mcqs.q: When meeting a teacher or stranger for the first time, do you use 'tu' or 'vous'?
options: Tu, because it's singular and you're talking to one person.
Either is fine in modern French.
